source_note: Burer, 'Robust Rankings for College Football', Journal of Quantitative Analysis in Sports 2012, Manuscript 1405 (Samuel Burer, University of Iowa), 22 pages. The first explicit robust football ranking: the Colley Matrix (one of six BCS computer rankings, the only fully published one) is shown sensitive to inconsequential-game outcomes (2010 LSU/Boise State flip from one omitted FCS game, BCS gap .0063), and a robust Colley Matrix Plus (CM+) variant is formulated as a min-max worst-case violation over a Gamma-budget of switched inconsequential games (bottom teams, win%<0.3). Key algebra: antisymmetric switch leaves C unchanged (schedule-only), b shifts linearly; the p=2 min-max reformulates to a strictly convex QP solved by cutting-plane constraint generation in <1 min (CPLEX). Switch measure (top-25 rank displacement) drops from CM mean 5.1/worst 20 to CM+ Gamma=5 mean 1.8/worst 10 (L=1). Data 2006-2011 (Wilson/Wolfe archive). Extracted faithfully (not a derivative summary). Equations 1-2 (Colley C/b), 3 (b perturbation), 4 (min-max), 6 (convex QP), the switch measure, and perturbation sets are printed in a shifted/custom math font that extracts garbled; reconstructed in labeled LaTeX and flagged here and in assumptions. Domain football matches catalog; American college football (FBS). The robust min-max rating formulation, Gamma conservatism budget (Bertsimas-Sim), schedule-invariant perturbation algebra, constraint-generation solver, switch-measure sensitivity metric, and signal-vs-noise selectivity are directly isomorphic to GSE's robust rating and sensitivity-analysis layer. No sportsbook lines/spreads/totals/implied odds in source or lifted into GSE.

reasoning_traces.think: The retrocausal genealogy of this paper is the importation of robust optimization into sports rankings. Samuel Burer, in the Department of Management Sciences at the University of Iowa, publishing in the Journal of Quantitative Analysis in Sports in 2012 as Manuscript 1405, takes the Colley Matrix, one of the six computer rankings used by the Bowl Championship Series and the only one fully published in the open literature, and asks whether its top rankings can be made robust. The motivation is concrete and slightly scandalous: at the end of the 2010 regular season, Colley's submitted rankings omitted a single Football Championship Subdivision playoff game between Appalachian State and Western Illinois, and because LSU and Boise State were separated by only six thousandths of a point in the overall BCS standings, that one omitted game flipped their order. The paper sits in the lineage of robust optimization from Ben-Tal, El Ghaoui, and Nemirovski, robust least-squares from El Ghaoui and Lebret, and the Bertsimas-Sim price-of-robustness budget, alongside ranking methods from Colley, Keener's Perron-Frobenius approach, and Massey. The recursive theory of mind is the Colley linear system and its perturbation algebra. The Colley matrix C equals two I plus the diagonal of the games-played vector minus the symmetric win matrix, and the right-hand side b equals the ones vector plus half the win-loss spread; C is diagonally dominant and positive definite, so the ratings r equal C inverse b are unique and sorted descending. The crucial structural insight is that switching a game's outcome is an antisymmetric perturbation Delta with Delta plus Delta transpose equal to zero, which leaves C unchanged because C depends only on the schedule, while b shifts linearly by half the antisymmetric part of Delta times the ones vector. The robust method, called Colley Matrix Plus, therefore seeks a single ratings vector minimizing the worst-case violation of the perturbed system over all scenarios that switch at most Gamma inconsequential games, where Gamma is a user-supplied conservatism budget and inconsequential games are those between bottom teams with winning percentage below zero point three. Cross-layer veto adjudication is the tractable reformulation and the empirical sensitivity comparison. The min-max problem with the two-norm is reformulated via an auxiliary variable into a strictly convex quadratic program with one linear constraint per scenario, which has a unique optimum and avoids the ambiguous alternative optima of the infinity-norm version; because the scenario set is exponentially large, a cutting-plane constraint-generation loop solves a subset, finds a violated constraint through a subproblem, and repeats until optimality is proved, all in under a minute with CPLEX. The sensitivity is measured by the switch measure, the sum of absolute rank changes among the top twenty-five teams: the basic Colley rankings show a mean switch of five point one and a worst case of twenty for a single switched game, while the robust rankings at Gamma five cut the mean to one point eight and the worst case to ten, with most per-instance bubble-chart points below the equality line and the worst-case tail particularly reduced. The implementation invariants map directly onto GSE. The Colley schedule-adjusted rating is GSE's strength-of-schedule rating solve; the Gamma budget is GSE's Bertsimas-Sim-style conservatism parameter; the min-max worst-case objective is GSE's robust-optimization formulation; the schedule-invariant C is GSE's structural-versus-data separation that makes robustness cheap; and the constraint-generation loop is GSE's cutting-plane scalability technique. The switch measure is GSE's ranking-sensitivity metric, and the distinction between protecting inconsequential games while remaining sensitive to important contender games is GSE's signal-versus-noise selectivity. The outputs are robust ratings from win-loss data; GSE lifts no sportsbook lines, spreads, totals, or implied odds. The behavioral results make the robustness concrete and honest. As Gamma increases from zero to ten in the 2008 season, no team moves more than two positions, changes occur within separate groups of closely ranked teams such as Utah and Texas Tech swapping, the top three of Oklahoma, Florida, and Texas retain their ranks throughout, and the rankings stabilize for Gamma between seven and ten; the two extremes are Gamma zero, identical to Colley and equally sensitive, and Gamma at least the total number of inconsequential games, completely insensitive because both the original and perturbed rankings optimize over the same all-switch scenario set. The author is candid that comparing two rankings objectively is hard without further analysis, and that Gamma eight is more robust than Gamma three only by construction. The caveats close the account with the scope and customization limits. The method protects against switched outcomes of inconsequential games, not omitted games, which the author argues can be prevented by careful data handling; it is non-stochastic, making no distributional assumptions and computing a single worst-case ranking rather than an average; and the inconsequential set is user-customizable, extendable to other sports, to including FCS games, or to protecting very close games decided by fewer than three points. The invariant for GSE is to carry the robust min-max rating formulation, the Gamma conservatism budget, the schedule-invariant perturbation algebra, and the constraint-generation solver while recording the non-stochastic worst-case scope, the subjective Gamma choice, and the difficulty of objectively comparing rankings before any quantitative reuse, treating robustness as protection of the top ratings against noise without dulling their response to genuine signal.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: Import robust optimization into sports rankings. Samuel Burer, U Iowa Management Sciences; JQAS 2012 Manuscript 1405. Colley Matrix (1 of 6 BCS computer rankings, only fully published). Motivation: 2010 omitted App State-W Illinois FCS game flipped LSU/Boise State (BCS gap .0063). Lineage: robust optimization (Ben-Tal/El Ghaoui/Nemirovski 2009), robust least-squares (El Ghaoui-Lebret 1997), Bertsimas-Sim price of robustness (2004); Colley/Keener Perron-Frobenius/Massey/Chartier sensitivity (2011). First explicit robust football ranking. CM+ method.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Colley C=2I+Diag((W+W^T)e)-(W+W^T) (Eq1), b=e+(1/2)(W-W^T)e (Eq2); C diag-dominant PD; r=C^-1 b sorted. W_ij=times i beat j; win-loss only (no points). Switch Delta antisymmetric (Delta+Delta^T=0) -> C'=C (schedule fixed), b'=b+(1/2)(Delta-Delta^T)e (Eq3). Inconsequential = bottom teams win%<omega=0.3; T=top 25. Robust min_r max_{Delta in D(Gamma)} ||Cr-b'||_p (Eq4, p=2; p=inf ambiguous). Aux t -> strictly convex QP (Eq6), one constraint/scenario, unique optimum. D(Gamma)=sum C(N,gamma); cutting-plane constraint generation. Switch measure delta=sum_{i in T}|pi_i-pi'_i|. CPLEX 12.2/Matlab <1 min. Equations shifted-font reconstructed.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: CM sensitivity: L=1 delta mean 5.1/median 4/max 20/stdev 4.9; L=2 mean 6.5/max 28. CM+ Gamma=5: L=1 mean 1.8/median 0/max 10/stdev 2.4; L=2 mean 2.5/max 14; bubble chart most below x=y; worst-case tail (CM 15-20 L=1/20-25 L=2) particularly reduced. Extremes: Gamma=0=CM (as sensitive); Gamma>=N completely insensitive (same all-switch scenario set). 2008 top-3 (Oklahoma/Florida/Texas) stable; top-15 mostly robust except Utah/Texas Tech; <=2 pos move; stabilize 7<=Gamma<=10. Marshall-Rice 2007 worst case delta=20; West Virginia 4-spot drop excessive. Non-stochastic worst-case; protects switches not omissions; custom I (close games <3 pts). Zero sportsbook lines lifted.

universal_lens: A robust-optimization treatment of the Colley Matrix college-football ranking shows the basic method is fragile to inconsequential games (one omitted FCS game flipped LSU and Boise State separated by 0.0063 in the BCS), and proposes Colley Matrix Plus: a min-max worst-case ratings solve over a user Gamma-budget of switched games between bottom teams, exploiting the fact that an antisymmetric outcome switch leaves the schedule-dependent Colley matrix unchanged and shifts only the right-hand side, reformulated as a strictly convex quadratic program solved by cutting-plane constraint generation in under a minute, which cuts the top-25 switch measure from a mean of 5.1 and worst case of 20 down to 1.8 and 10 while preserving sensitivity to important contender games.
gsi_mapping: GSI treats Colley C=2I+Diag((W+W^T)e)-(W+W^T)/b=e+(1/2)(W-W^T)e (Eqs1-2), C PD, r=C^-1 b; win-loss only (BCS, no points); motivation 2010 LSU/Boise flip (omitted FCS game, gap .0063); robustness = top rankings stable vs inconsequential (bottom teams win%<0.3) switches, still sensitive to contender games; Gamma>=0 conservatism budget (Bertsimas-Sim 2004), Gamma=0=CM, Gamma>=N completely insensitive; non-stochastic worst-case; antisymmetric Delta -> C'=C, b'=b+(1/2)(Delta-Delta^T)e (Eq3); min_r max_{D(Gamma)} ||Cr-b'||_p (Eq4, p=2); aux-t strictly convex QP (Eq6) unique optimum; D(Gamma)=sum C(N,gamma) cutting-plane constraint generation; switch measure delta=sum_{i in T}|pi_i-pi'_i| (top 25); CM L=1 mean 5.1/max 20 vs CM+ Gamma=5 mean 1.8/max 10; bubble below x=y; worst-case tail reduced; 2008 top-3 stable/top-15 mostly robust; <1 min CPLEX; data 2006-2011 Wilson/Wolfe (2010 n=195); equations shifted-font reconstructed.
gse_mapping: GSE lifts the robust min-max rating formulation, the Gamma conservatism budget, the schedule-invariant perturbation algebra (C fixed, b linear), the strictly-convex-QP-plus-constraint-generation solver, and the switch-measure sensitivity metric as its robust rating and sensitivity-analysis layer; treats the protection of inconsequential games while preserving contender-game sensitivity as signal-vs-noise selectivity, the non-stochastic worst-case scope and subjective Gamma choice as honest limits, and the difficulty of objectively comparing rankings as a validation caveat; all outputs are robust ratings from win-loss data, never sportsbook lines, and robustness protects top ratings against noise without dulling their response to genuine signal.
